summary:
I've built module M2 (users, team and access links) as briefed. Type-check, lint and all 89 new unit tests pass, and I didn't touch any file outside my ownership list. Nothing was run against the live Supabase project.

**Library (`src/lib/auth-admin/`).** Everything in the brief is there:
- **Links:** `createAccessLink`, `revokeAccessLink`, `listPendingAccessLinks`.
- **Auth accounts:** `ensureAuthUser`, `setUserBanned` ("876000h" / "none"), `resetUserMfa`, `listAuthUsers` (paged, with last sign-in and 2FA status).
- **Accept page:** `previewAccessLink`, `claimAccessLink` and `signInWithEmailLink`.
- **Audit:** `issueLinkWithAudit` logs every new link as the acting user; if the log entry fails, the link is revoked again. A 2FA reset is logged before the authenticators are removed.
- **Links:** a token is 32 random bytes; only its sha256 hex is stored. An earlier pending link for the same person and purpose is revoked only after the new one exists, so a refused request never kills a working link. Tokens are never logged.
- The pure parts (tokens, links, users) don't import `server-only`, so the command-line script can reuse them.

**`/access/[token]` (public).**
- **Opening the link:** only looks up who it's for. It shows the ScaleUp logo, the person's name and email, the expiry, and an "Accept invitation" or "Sign in" button. It never signs anyone in and never touches the visitor's current session.
- **Pressing the button:** rate-limits per IP, then claims the link atomically with `claim_access_link` before anything else. Only then does it sign the person in (`generateLink` magic link, then `verifyOtp` with type `magiclink`), start the idle clock and redirect.
- **Invalid or used links:** they get a clear message, for example "This link has expired or was already used. Ask ScaleUp (or your company owner) for a new one." A link that was claimed stays used even if signing in then fails.
- **Bare `/access`:** redirects to `/login`.

**`/admin/users` (Super Admin only).** Three tabs: ScaleUp team, Company users and Pending invitations. Each has search; the company tab also has a company filter.
- **Columns:** name with email and job title, role or company memberships, status, 2FA and last sign-in.
- **Invitations:** "Invite ScaleUp user" and "Invite company user" both end in a dialog showing the link, a Copy button, the expiry and "send it by email or chat".
- **Row actions:** edit name, job title and role; manage company access (change role, deactivate or reactivate a membership); add to a company; a new invitation link or a sign-in link; reset 2FA; deactivate or reactivate the account (profile change plus ban, and pending links revoked).
- **Pending links:** can be revoked from the Pending invitations tab.
- **Role mixing:** a company user's email can't become ScaleUp staff, and vice versa; the form shows the reason under the email field.
- **Deletion:** nobody can be deleted.
- `?company=<id>` opens the company tab filtered to that company.

**`/portal/[companyId]/team`.**
- **Owners of an active company:** can invite contributors, send new invitation or sign-in links, revoke links they or a co-owner sent, and deactivate or reactivate contributors.
- **When the database refuses an owner's link:** this happens when the person also reaches another company. The person is still added and the owner is told to ask them to sign in as usual (or ask ScaleUp for a link).
- **Contributors and exited or written-off companies:** read-only.
- **Links sent by ScaleUp:** shown as "from ScaleUp", never by name.

**`scripts/create-user.ts`.** New people get no password; the script prints a one-time `/access` invitation link (7 days). People who never signed in get a fresh invitation link. The new `--sign-in-link` flag prints a 24-hour sign-in link for an existing account. Setting a password for automated test users still works via `--password-stdin` or `CREATE_USER_PASSWORD`. Reactivating with `--force` now also lifts the sign-in ban. Links from the script are recorded in the audit log.

**Things to check at integration.**
- 2FA status comes from Supabase's user list including authenticator details. If the hosted project doesn't return them, the code falls back to asking per account (5 at a time). Worth one look on the real project.
- Supabase's auth library throws, rather than returns an error, for ids that aren't UUIDs. All my inputs are validated UUIDs, but other modules should know.
- Sign-in links go through 2FA and then to setting a new password, not just to `/mfa`. This departs from the contract; the reason is in the deviations list.
deviations: The /access accept action sends sign-in links to /mfa?next=/set-password rather than plain /mfa (invitations still go to /set-password). A sign-in link is how a forgotten password is recovered (BRD B23). With plain /mfa the person ends up signed in but still without a password they know; they could only change it from the account menu within 15 minutes. The link is still claimed first, then generateLink, verifyOtp with type 'magiclink' and startIdleClock, exactly as the contract says.

createAccessLink returns { id, userId, purpose, url, expiresAt } (a superset of { url, expiresAt }). Expiry is 7 days or 24 hours minus a 1-minute margin, so it always stays inside the database cap (access_links_max_validity), which counts from the database's own clock.

The GET lookup on /access/[token] reads access_links plus an embedded profile (email, full_name, is_active) with the service role. This follows the contract's 'read-only lookup by token hash … who it is for'. Only a valid link reveals the person.

Owners may revoke only pending links sent by an owner of their company. Links sent by ScaleUp show as 'from ScaleUp' on the Team page and are revoked by ScaleUp. Owners may also send new invitation or sign-in links to their contributors (allowed by B29; the database guard decides, and its 42501 message is shown as-is).

Inviting someone who has already signed in (Super Admin company invite or owner invite) adds or reactivates the membership without issuing a link. The person gets a notice to sign in as usual, and an 'invite' audit event is logged with link_issued: false.
Deactivating an account (Super Admin) also revokes its pending links. When an owner deactivates a contributor, the pending links that the company's owners sent them are revoked.

Audit ordering: invite and sign_in_link are logged right after the link is created; if logging fails, the link is revoked and the error shown, so no usable link is ever unrecorded. mfa_reset is logged before the factors are removed. All events use entity 'profiles' with the account id as entity_id.

listAuthUsers() relies on Supabase's user list including factors. If none are reported at all, it asks per signed-in account (mfa.listFactors, 5 at a time); if that also fails, 2FA shows as unknown ('—').

scripts/create-user.ts: a password on the command line (--password) is still refused, as in the foundation script. 'Keep --password for automated test users' is implemented as the existing --password-stdin and CREATE_USER_PASSWORD. Added --sign-in-link; --force reactivation now also lifts the sign-in ban; links from the script are logged as system events. ARCHITECTURE §4 lists this file under F-AUTH, but my brief assigned it to M2.

The pure helpers under src/lib/auth-admin (tokens, purpose, links, users, status, schemas, types) do not import 'server-only', so the plain-tsx script and Client Components can use them. The service-role wrappers index.ts and audit.ts do import it. Shared M2 client components live in src/app/access/_components/ and are imported by /admin/users and the Team page.

Page props are typed explicitly as the brief requires, not with the PageProps globals. I also added error.tsx to both pages (Next 16 retry()), loading.tsx to all three routes, and /access without a token redirects to /login.
openQuestions: Confirm that sign-in links should lead through two-factor authentication to choosing a new password (/mfa?next=/set-password) rather than plain /mfa. I recommend it for B23 (forgotten password). The downside: someone who still knows their password but receives a sign-in link must pick a new one.
Confirm the owner revoke scope: owners can revoke only links sent by an owner of their company; links sent by ScaleUp can be revoked only by ScaleUp.
Please verify once on the hosted project that auth.admin.listUsers includes 'factors', so the 2FA column is accurate without the per-account fallback.
When a Super Admin adds an existing, already-signed-in account to another company, no link is issued; a sign-in link can be sent from the row menu. Is that the desired default?

Should owners see the pending-link status and sender for co-owners too? Currently any pending link of any team member is shown ('Sign-in link from ScaleUp, expires …'), with no names of ScaleUp staff.
notesForOtherModules: Routes exposed by M2: GET /access/[token] (public; its Server Action acceptAccessLinkAction lives in src/app/access/[token]/actions.ts); /access → /login; /admin/users (requireScaleUp(['super_admin'])) with ?tab=scaleup|company|pending and ?company=<companyId> (opens Company users filtered to that company and preselects it in 'Invite company user'); /portal/[companyId]/team (every member; owners of an active company manage it). The proxy already treats /access as public and self-managed; no change needed.

M1 (companies): link the company page's people/team section to `/admin/users?company=${companyId}` (optionally `&tab=company`). Invitations and membership changes happen there, so M1 does not need to call M2 code.

Integrator / contract (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): update the §4 ownership table (scripts/create-user.ts now M2 per this brief), the §2.2 flow and the §4 /access line (sign-in links → /mfa?next=/set-password), and §5 with the new shared API. Server-only (src/lib/auth-admin index): createAccessLink({userId,purpose,createdBy}) → {id,userId,purpose,url,expiresAt}; revokeAccessLink(id); revokeUserAccessLinks(userId,{purpose?,createdBy?}); getAccessLink(id); listPendingAccessLinks({userIds?}); previewAccessLink(token); claimAccessLink(token); signInWithEmailLink(email); ensureAuthUser({email,fullName}); getAuthUser(id); setUserBanned(id,banned); resetUserMfa(id); listAuthUsers(); getSiteUrl(); isOwnerLinkRefusal. src/lib/auth-admin/audit.ts: logAccessEvent, issueLinkWithAudit. Client-safe: purpose.ts, status.ts, schemas.ts, types.ts.

Integrator / BRD §13 (not in my ownership): consider adding build decisions: (a) a sign-in link (B23) leads through the authenticator check to choosing a new password; (b) owners revoke only the links they or a co-owner sent, and ScaleUp revokes its own; (c) inviting someone who already signed in just adds them, with no link.
All modules: auth-js admin methods (getUserById, updateUserById, mfa.listFactors/deleteFactor) THROW, rather than return an error, for ids that aren't UUIDs. Validate ids before calling them.

F-AUTH (FYI, nothing to change): the Team page, admin page and /access use AuthShell, IdleTimer only where already mounted, toActionError, assertScaleUp/assertCompanyAccess/requireScaleUp/requireCompanyAccess, startIdleClock, RATE_LIMITS.emailLinkPerIp and canManageCompanyTeam/membershipFor as-is.

Operations: to bootstrap the first Super Admin, run `npm run user:create -- --email kenneth@scaleup.my --name "Kenneth Siew" --role super_admin`. It prints a one-time /access invitation link (7 days) built from NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL in .env.local. Add `--sign-in-link` for a 24-hour sign-in link to an existing account; use `--password-stdin` or CREATE_USER_PASSWORD only for automated test users.
